sources.supports: Every method validates its identifier and places it as the only path segment of the matching endpoint. updateLabel additionally validates payload.project_id, and deleteLabels checks that label_ids is a non-empty array and validates every member, so those two payload rules are the driver's rather than the boundary's alone. The reads parse against LabelSchema, the two writes against LabelWriteResponseSchema, and the two deletes pass no schema and resolve with no value.

The reference documents get_label, get_labels and update_label only. get_labels takes the project plus limit and offset and no other filter. update_label takes project_id and title, both required, and caps the title at 20 characters. It documents neither add_label, delete_label nor delete_labels, so those three rest on the driver and on the official TestRail CLI.

The official TestRail CLI reads a label mutation's reply as label_data.get('label', label_data), handling both the wrapped and the flat form, and sends add and update as the driver does. It enforces the 20-character title cap in its own command layer rather than relying on the server.

input_policy.notes: The endpoint takes one identifier in the path and no request body at all, so every field beyond it is refused. TestRail's Labels reference documents neither this endpoint nor the two other label writes; the driver and the official TestRail CLI are the evidence that it exists and what it sends.

outer_result.notes: The method resolves with no value and the wrapper reports data: null. Deleting a label removes it from every case and test carrying it and cannot be undone.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Send exactly one request. The adapter never follows up with further calls to find or repair what the deletion removed.

parameters.semantics: The label to delete. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as the only path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.
